subject.title: Feature: Streaming TTS pipeline for voice calls (sentence-level LLM→TTS→audio)

question: Should OpenClaw add a provider-generic telephony streaming contract for the classic voice-call STT-to-LLM-to-TTS path, and what fallback/provider semantics should it require?
rationale: The missing capability is clear from source, but the permanent API shape affects bundled and external speech providers, Twilio/Telnyx playback adapters, fallback behavior, and user-visible latency expectations.

options.title: Design additive provider-generic streaming
options.body: Add a telephony audio stream capability to the speech/plugin SDK, wire sentence-level text delivery through voice-call, and keep buffered synthesis as fallback for unsupported providers.

options.title: Use realtime voice as the low-latency path
options.body: Document realtime voice as the supported low-latency solution and leave the classic STT-to-LLM-to-TTS path buffered.

options.title: Approve a narrow provider experiment
options.body: Allow a Twilio/OpenAI or ElevenLabs-first implementation, with follow-up API work required before Telnyx and other providers can share it.

recommendation.title: Design additive provider-generic streaming
recommendation.body: Add a telephony audio stream capability to the speech/plugin SDK, wire sentence-level text delivery through voice-call, and keep buffered synthesis as fallback for unsupported providers.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans voice-call product behavior and plugin SDK surface, and the strongest cross-boundary history signal is steipete.
